headings.title: Introduction and Purpose of Family Planning Records
headings.content: Record keeping in family planning involves the systematic documentation of client interactions, medical histories, contraceptive choices, and follow-up schedules. These records serve as a permanent clinical memory for healthcare providers working in busy Nigerian health facilities, ensuring continuity of care when different nurses attend to the same client during subsequent visits. Accurate records track contraceptive continuation rates, identify side effects early, and provide vital data for local health authorities to forecast commodity supplies like injectables, implants, and oral pills.

headings.title: Core Components of a Client File and Registers
headings.content:
A comprehensive family planning client file contains specific clinical and demographic data gathered during consultations. Clinic registers complement individual folders by capturing daily service statistics.

- **Client Demographic Data**: Full name, age, address, marital status, and occupation.
- **Medical and Reproductive History**: Past pregnancies, menstrual history, chronic illnesses, and previous contraceptive use.
- **Physical Assessment Findings**: Blood pressure readings, weight, and results of physical or pelvic examinations.
- **Method Chosen**: The specific contraceptive method selected and informed consent documentation.
- **Continuation and Follow-up Schedule**: Dates for subsequent clinic visits, resupply dates, or removal appointments.

headings.title: Principles of Accurate Documentation
headings.content: Good nursing documentation follows strict professional standards to ensure clarity, legibility, and legal protection. Nurses must record entries promptly after client interactions rather than relying on memory at the end of a shift. Every entry must be factual, objective, and free from personal bias or judgmental language regarding a client's family size or lifestyle choices. If an error occurs in a paper record, the nurse should draw a single neat line through the mistake, write the correct information, and sign beside it without using correction fluid.

headings.title: Confidentiality, Privacy, and Data Protection
headings.content: Family planning clients share highly sensitive personal, marital, and reproductive information under the assumption of absolute privacy. Nurses have a legal and ethical duty to safeguard physical records by keeping them locked in cabinets when not in use and closing electronic databases when stepping away from a computer terminal. Breaching confidentiality by discussing a client's contraceptive choice with family members or community members destroys trust, violates professional codes of conduct, and deters vulnerable individuals from seeking necessary reproductive health services.

headings.title: Legal and Ethical Responsibilities of the Nurse
headings.content: In Nigerian healthcare practice, clinical records serve as legal documents in courts of law. The legal maxim 'if it was not charted, it was not done' underscores the reality that unrecorded nursing actions carry no legal proof during malpractice investigations or litigations. Nurses must ensure that informed consent is clearly documented before administering any procedure or dispensing long-acting reversible contraceptives like implants or intrauterine devices, confirming that the client understood the benefits, risks, and side effects.
